title: tokens-logs: Cloud Logging → Loki pipeline lagging

model.expr: quantile_over_time(0.5, {service="tokens-logs-pipeline", env="prd"} | json | event="gcp_logs_push" | unwrap lag_s [10m]) by ()

annotations.summary: Most Cloud Run logs are reaching Loki more than 5 minutes late (or the pipeline heartbeat has stopped)
annotations.description: The admin service's /hooks/gcp-logs push writes a heartbeat straight to Loki with every push: lag_s is how old the oldest entry in that push was (Cloud Logging → sink → Pub/Sub → push → Loki), publish_lag_s the same measured from the Pub/Sub publish time. This rule fires when the MEDIAN lag_s over 10 minutes stays above 300 s for 10 minutes, i.e. more than half of all pushes are behind, or when no heartbeat at all has been seen for 10 minutes. It deliberately ignores a tail: on 2026-10-28 Google's Logs Router delivered 1–3 % of entries 4–6 min late in both projects all afternoon while everything else landed within seconds, and the previous max-based rule flapped on that for hours. While this fires every Loki-based 'silent/stale' rule is looking at data that has not arrived yet; those rules carry a 600 s lag guard and stay quiet, so a real job outage during a lag episode surfaces only once the backlog drains. Causes so far: a daily 400k–600k-entry Postgres NOTICE burst from tokens-assets-prd-us (2026-10-24/26/27, fixed at the source) that backed up tokens-logs-to-grafana-prd behind the admin service's 10-instance ceiling. Check: lag_s vs publish_lag_s in the heartbeat (large gap = Logs Router, Google's side; large publish_lag_s = Pub/Sub backlog or hook 502s), Pub/Sub num_undelivered_messages / oldest_unacked_message_age on tokens-logs-to-grafana-prd, admin 429 'no available instance' counts, then log_entry_count by service+severity to find a burst source. Recipe in docs/operations/log-pipeline.md.
